title: Testing: unit tests, UI tests, and previews as a working tool

videos.script: This is the one lesson about iOS apps that runs almost entirely on Linux. {{tests}} A test is a program that knows the answer. You write the planner's tests in Swift Testing, the framework the Swift toolchain ships everywhere. {{suite}} A suite for the week's total. {{params}} One test with ten arguments, for the days where calendars break: a new year, a leap day, a Sunday. {{fail}} Then you break the code on purpose, and read exactly which cases fail and by how much. {{async}} An async test, with a fake source that fails every time. {{xctest}} The same checks in XCTest, which every Xcode project already has. {{ui}} On a Mac, UI tests drive the app from outside, and previews show a screen in every state. Those two are not run here. {{coverage}} And coverage, measured once. It points at two lines no test has ever run, and that is worth more than the percentage.
